newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures end lower after late selloff.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures end lower after late selloff.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended lower Thursday in a lackluster session, hit by some technical selling and long liquidation when upside momentum stalled early despite a steady cash, industry sources said.
December slipped 4.1 cents to close at $2.643 per million British thermal units. January settled 2.9 cents lower at $2.649. Other deferreds ended down by one-half to 1.6 cents.

"People jumped (bought) early on the revised (cold) weather forecasts, but we really don't have the weather to support these prices," said one Midwest trader, adding funds rolling length out of December also helped pressure the complex.

Despite deteriorating technicals, traders said near-term forecasts for colder East Coast weather could limit the downside. But they said without sustained cold, any rally will continue to be a struggle.
Chartists pegged next support in December in the $2.52-2.53 area, with resistance seen at $2.745 and then at the $2.88 contract high.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices held steady Thursday at about $2.70. Midwest prices were flat to up slightly at about $2.60. Forecasts for cold weather this weekend kept New York city gate gas prices in the mid-$2.90s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell 1.6 cents to $2.165. NYMEX said 31,333 Hub contracts traded, down from Wednesday's revised tally of 36,759.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas closed 1.5 cents higher at a new contract high of $1.27, while deferreds settled mixed. NYMEX said 20 Alberta contracts traded versus five on Wednesday.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded but December ended two cents lower at $2.49.

On the KCBT, December finished three cents lower at $2.49, while deferreds settled down by one to five cents. The December East/West spread narrowed by 1.1 cents to 15.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 364 contracts traded, up from Wednesday's total of 242.
